title: Rendille Camel Milk Porridge
author: Mama Wanjiru

heritage.origin: Marsabit County — Rendille traditional lands, Northern Kenya
heritage.history: The Rendille are known as the "people of the camel." Camel milk is central to Rendille diet and culture — consumed fresh, fermented, and incorporated into porridge. Camel milk porridge has sustained the Rendille in one of Kenya's most arid regions for generations.
heritage.modernEvolution: Camel milk is gaining global attention for its nutritional properties and is now commercially produced in Northern Kenya.

desc: Rendille Camel Milk Porridge — finger millet or sorghum flour cooked in camel milk into a warm, nourishing, slightly tangy porridge. The daily breakfast of the Rendille people — a window into Northern Kenya's remarkable camel culture.
longDesc: Camel milk has a distinctive flavour — slightly saltier and richer in certain nutrients than cow milk. When used to make porridge instead of water, it creates something extraordinary.
ingredients: 1 cup finger millet flour or sorghum flour
3 cups camel milk (substitute: whole cow milk with a touch of salt)

substitutions.alternative: Whole cow milk — the flavour is milder but the method is identical

steps: Mix flour with 1 cup of cold camel milk to a smooth slurry.
Bring remaining 2 cups of camel milk and water to a gentle simmer.
Pour the flour slurry into the simmering milk, stirring constantly.
Stir over medium-low heat for 8—10 minutes until thick and smooth.
Add honey or sugar. Taste and adjust.
chefTips: Always make a cold milk slurry first.
Camel milk is naturally slightly saltier — reduce any added salt.
Stir constantly once the slurry is added.
commonMistakes: Not making a slurry — lumpy porridge.
cookingScience: Camel milk has a different protein structure from cow milk — smaller fat globules and different casein composition. It does not curdle as readily when heated, making it particularly suitable for cooking.
sustainabilityTips: Camels produce milk even in extreme drought conditions.
reheating: Warm gently with a splash of milk, stirring.
healthBenefits: Camel milk contains higher vitamin C and iron than cow milk.
Lower lactose than cow milk — more digestible.
Finger millet provides calcium and iron.
culturalNote: The Rendille are Kenya's most iconic camel people — a community whose entire way of life is structured around the camel.
